doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Eddie Cole's toilet-seat act and the limburger prank
summary: Black entertainment for white clientele; Nat Cole's brother Eddie and Terry's limburger prank.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Was [ ? ? ] where there was black entertainment for whites only?

Black entertainment and white clientele, all the time, all the time, until Nat “King” Cole’s brother had an act called the Three Loose Nuts. He worked there. He did an act where he put a toilet seat around his head and . . .
No, this is Eddie. Eddie Cole. There’s Freddie, Eddie, and Nat, Nathaniel.

He put this toilet seat around his head. He put his head through the toilet seat. The lid would be in the back, and it had this long, operatic robe, like a – he would come up and sing [Terry imitates an opera singer], like opera. His opening line was to come out with this thing around his neck. He said, “Smells like somebody’s been using this damn thing today.” On one particular occasion, we put limburger cheese all over it.
